messages:
devin: seeing a sudden spike in retries and CPU/GPU queueing on model-service v4 in us-west-2. Traffic looks uneven — a few endpoints at 90% cpu, others almost idle. start time ~08:02 UTC. anyone else?
maya: saw the alert. ipvs stats show heavy conn count on two nodes only. could be hash skew or sticky connections.
jonathan: which kube-proxy mode are we on for that cluster? ipvs or iptables?
lina: ipvs. kube-proxy DaemonSet on that cluster got a kernel upgrade on nodepool last night.
devin: confirmed: kube-proxy ipvs. attaching quick output:
---
# ipvsadm -L -n --stats | grep model-service
TCP  10.1.45.12:8080 rr  persistent 0
  -> 10.48.3.12:8080            Masq    1000   3000  0 0
  -> 10.48.3.15:8080            Masq     50   1500  0 0
  -> 10.48.4.22:8080            Masq     45    800  0 0
---
maya: whoa. weights are wildly different (1000 vs 50). but our endpoints are created by k8s without explicit weights. ipvs internal hashing must be skewing.
sre-bot: incident created: INC-2026-234; assigning eng-infra.
jonathan: possible causes: MTU mismatch causing fragmentation and packet drops on some hosts -> connections failover to fewer endpoints; or ipvs hash seed changed after kernel update and some endpoints mapped heavily.
lina: checked `dmesg` on the 10.48.3.12 host — saw repeated RX dropped and mtu warnings after the kernel update: "IPv4: packet too big for interface, mtu=1450"
ops-jen: those three nodes (3.12, 3.15, 4.22) are on different NIC firmware revisions. 3.12 had an SR-IOV vf driver update.
devin: that matches. if VF offloads differ, we can get asymmetric path/segmentation behaviour and ipvs may prefer certain hash buckets.
maya: quick checks we should run: `ethtool -k <iface>`, `ip link show`, `tracepath` between nodes, `cat /proc/net/ip_vs` and `ipvsadm -Ln --stats`. also check conntrack entries for service.
jonathan: i ran tracepath between 3.12 and 3.15: shows mtu drop to 1400 in between for 3.12 path only.
ops-jen: sounds like MTU discovery issues; maybe PMTU blackhole with RDMA/eni offload combos.
lina: workaround: set kube-proxy to use "sh" scheduler to spread? ipvs scheduler options we can tweak but it's brittle. better immediate mitigation: add a small headroom in service endpoints by adding a temporary endpoint replica on an underutilized node and adjust ipvs weights manually to rebalance.
devin: also enable our Redwood Console fallback: route 10% to model-service-v3 (lower-cap) to shed load while infra rollback proceeds.
sre-bot: action item logged: run mtudisc tests on affected nodepool, compare ethtool offloads, and roll back the kernel on nodepool-3 if confirmed.
jonathan: note — ipvs hash table can be rebalanced by restarting kube-proxy, but that will cause ephemeral churn. if kernel update changed hash seed, restarting alone may not help long-term.
maya: plan: 1) add temporary replica on healthy nodes (devin), 2) run ethtool/mtudisc checks (ops-jen + lina), 3) limit sessionAffinity for service to None for 10m to force rehashing (jonathan), 4) open ticket with NIC vendor if driver/firmware mismatch (ops-jen).
ops-jen: I'll start MTU & offload checks now and post findings. pulling ethtool -k + sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward values.
devin: added replica and toggled canary in Console to route 10% to v3. retries dropped slightly but still high.
lina: ops-jen found that 3.12 has GSO disabled (`gso: off`) while others have it on. that explains fragmentation and heavier conn retry patterns on certain backends.
jonathan: who flipped GSO? that was from the vendor kernel package upgrade last night. rollback path?
ops-jen: rolling nodepool-3 back to previous kernel patch now (cordon + drain + kubelet restart). will take ~12m.
sre-bot: postmortem note placeholder created.
maya: good. long-term: we should add a CI check on nodepool image diffs for offload settings and add a kube-proxy health probe that surface endpoint weight skew beyond threshold.
devin: agreed. one-off fixes in flight; will monitor.
jonathan: if retries persist after rollback, next step is to temporarily switch kube-proxy to iptables on the nodepool as a safer scheduler while we validate.
lina: update 08:37 UTC: nodepool-3 rollbacks done, GSO restored, ipvs endpoint distribution rebalanced. CPU/GPU queues back to expected spread.
devin: metrics look good, retries back to baseline. closing incident once we verify 30m stability. :white_check_mark:
ops-jen: will follow up with vendor for driver patch and prepare a runbook for kernel rollbacks that includes checking offload flags.
maya: adding runbook item to eng-infra wiki and an alert to Console that triggers when ipvs per-endpoint weight ratio > 8x.
kubebot: reminder: please attach all command outputs and node IDs to INC-2026-234 for compliance.
devin: attaching logs and ethtool outputs to the incident now. thanks all.
